answer: Graders are drawn by verifiable random sampling from a registry of established identities that post bonded stake. Each task goes to a random quorum of five; two-thirds agreement with a blinded reference pays. Selection is unpredictable and weighted by standing, so a sparrow cannot pick its vine and an attacker cannot know which judges to bribe. Forging a vertex of influence needs many aged, staked identities just to seed one quorum, and any collusion proof slashes the bond. One sybil is cheap; a controlling quorum is ruinous.
